text:
maya: quick question — we need a practical pattern for handling PII in traces/spans. operations wants searchable telemetry but security wants no raw PHI in the hot store. thoughts? :thinking:

sree: do we mean remove/obfuscate attributes at ingest, or keep encrypted raw blobs for audits? both have tradeoffs.

maya: leaning toward attribute-level tokenization + short hot retention and a locked cold archive for raw spans (audit-only). wondering about keying model (per-customer vs global) and access workflow.

ash: cost note — keeping raw spans even cold is expensive (eg high-cardinality attributes). we should combine aggressive sampling + error-triggered full-capture.

ash: also: cardinality explosion if we hash IDs without stable mapping. makes joins / debug painful. :grimacing:

sree: propose pipeline: 1) Otel collector attribute processor to wipe/transform sensitive keys (email, phone, SSN) 2) replace with short token HMAC(attribute, rotation_key_id) 3) store encrypted raw span in a cold blob store with envelope encryption and KMS per-tenant key. 4) access via audited, gated API that requires approval.

sree: rough otel config sketch:
```yaml
processors:
  attributes/redact_sensitive:
    actions:
      - key: user.email
        action: hash  # or remove
      - key: user.ssn
        action: delete
  batch:
    timeout: 10s
exporters:
  otlp/secure_archive:
    endpoint: https://telemetry-archive.internal
    auth: workload-identity
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes/redact_sensitive, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/secure_archive, logging]
```

tara: security + compliance perspective: this is reasonable but must satisfy two things: (1) decryption of raw spans for audits must be auditable & require two-person approval (2) retention TTLs must be policy-driven per-data-class and exportable for compliance reports. Also prefer per-tenant KMS for isolating risk. :lock:

maya: two-person approval adds friction — can we gate by roles (security,sre) and ticket ID? maybe a short-lived signed token to decrypt for dev investigation.

sree: implementation note: store envelope key metadata with the span blob, KMS handles DEK, and our audit service emits a signed ticket when decryption is performed. Also rotate HMAC keys quarterly.

ash: sampling rules we should consider: keep full traces on errors (5xx, traces with anomaly score > threshold), and for normal requests keep N% random traces per customer, configurable. need per-tenant override.

maya: operational concerns: queryability — hashed tokens make debugging cross-service flows harder. need a secure lookup service to map tokens back to original attributes for authorized investigations. that lookup itself is sensitive.

tara: yes — the lookup should only return redacted context and be behind JIT approval. log every lookup with the requester, reason, and TTL. compliance will audit monthly.

sec-bot: reminder — from policy: telemetry containing regulated data (PII/PHI) must not be retained in hot store beyond 30 days unless explicit risk approval. See https://redwood.internal/policy/telemetry-data-retention

sree: action items I can take: prototype attribute processor + HMAC, wire a stash export to encrypted archive, and mock a JIT approval flow for decryption. estimate 2 sprints.

maya: perfect. ash — can you draft sampling thresholds and cost model for cold retention?

ash: on it. will share numbers by EOD tomorrow.

maya: tara — can you draft the approval workflow SLOs and audit fields we need?

tara: will do.

deploy-bot: deployment queued: otel-collector/redact-attr-proto -> canary at 2023-11-02T14:20Z :rocket:

maya: thanks all. summary: attribute-level tokenization + encrypted cold archive + audited JIT decryption + sampling. we'll iterate on keys (per-tenant vs org) after prototype. :thumbsup:
